thread.title: DSG extends library hours, approves over $16,000 in funding

author: Dylan Halper
title: DSG extends library hours, approves over $16,000 in funding
text:
Duke Student Government Senators briefly met Wednesday to approve funding allocations and provided committee updates. The Senate quickly went into an impeachment hearing.
Committee updates
Senators from the academic affairs committee announced that the hours of study spaces in the David M. Rubenstein Rare Book & Manuscript Library and von der Heyden will be extended to 3 a.m. on weekdays and midnight on weekends.
The services and sustainability committee launched a new “Devil’s Playground” initiative. Every Friday from March 27 to April 17, recreation equipment will be free for students to rent on Abele Quad from 3 p.m. to 5 p.m. This includes footballs, soccer balls, spikeball sets, picnic blankets, frisbees and volleyballs.
The committee also announced there will be a “Blue Devil Market,” an opportunity for undergraduate and graduate students to acquire free produce and fruit sourced from local vendors. The market will be on April 3 from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m.
The campus life committee is working to revise the undergraduate housing portal. They have scheduled meetings with Housing and Residence Life.
First-year Noah Bean, a senator of the Durham and community affairs committee, announced that its passport initiative launched this week.
SOFC updates
Senators approved the following SOFC allocations.
Duke Catholic Center: $2,600 out of its requested $3,000 to cover catering costs for its Easter Sunday brunch April 5.
Devils En Pointe: $2,033 out of its requested $2,394 to cover space rental and guest travel costs for its showcase on April 11 in partnership with Embodiment Dance Company.
Duke Business Behind Heath: $4,351 out of its requested $5,857 to cover costs for its “The New Health Order” conference on April 11.
Project Tadpole: $5,303 funded in full to cover catering, speaker and space rental costs for its Accessibility at Duke Expo on April 13.
Runway of Dreams: $2,392 funded in full to cover equipment and space rental costs for its Adaptive Fashion Show event on April 7.
In other business
The internal vote for the Chief Financial Officer position was pushed back an additional week to April 1 due to the closed proceeding on impeachment.
